title: GTA 6 Launch Leads to Special Holiday for All Palworld Dev Employees
text: GTA 6 Launch Leads to Special Holiday for All Palworld Dev Employees | Push Square Menu Search Share Guest Guest Login | Sign Up Push Square News Reviews Features Videos Games PS Plus Guides Forums Search Keywords Guest Login or Sign Up Home Choose Topics... Manage Topics News Pocketpair Rockstar Games PS5 GTA GTA 6 Launch Leads to Special Holiday for All Palworld Dev Employees Leonida here we come by Stephen Tailby 4 hours ago Share: Image: Push Square GTA 6 launches in one week's time, and the anticipation and excitement for the game is hard to ignore. Rockstar Games' inbound open world action game is going to be a major cultural event when it launches on 19th November, and it seems some companies are recognising that — most notably, Pocketpair, the team behind Palworld . The Japanese studio has announced that all employees are officially entitled to a period of leave from 19th to 23rd November so they can enjoy GTA 6 over an uninterrupted five days. All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA6 launches. Please see the attached notice for details. pic.twitter.com/qJjJ7IvhhY - Palworld (@Palworld_EN) November 12, 2026 "On November 19, millions of gamers around the world will find themselves sitting at school or work, gazing longingly out the window, knowing that a new era of gaming is about to begin," the statement reads. "At Pocketpair, we believe that such a historic occasion deserves our full attention. Therefore, after careful consideration, we have decided that all employees who intend to play Grand Theft Auto VI will be granted a special five-day holiday." It's a move that's going down extremely well on social media, as you'd expect. GTA 6 is reportedly causing a big spike in employees taking annual leave, with US employers estimated to lose a combined $1 billion of business on the 19th thanks to staff staying home to play. Pocketpair isn't the only company offering time off; Logitech has announced Logi Game Day, an initiative that grants all employees a single day off for the purpose of playing video games. While this can be used at any point over the next 12 months, the timing of its arrival suggests it's been implemented with GTA 6 in mind. A while ago, a smaller business, Burger Motorsports, announced its intention to observe a day off for the game too. It seems there are some businesses out there trying to get ahead of the curve. For what is almost certainly the biggest game of the decade, I think it's a smart move. Related Articles Poll Are You Taking Time Off for GTA 6? But, whilst the first few games deserved that to a degree (even if I didn't think they were all amazing games), in that they had systems/mechanics/style etc that went on to inspire other games, I don't think the later games were all that inspiring. The same argument of 'impact' be made for a lot of games that heavily inspired others, and your argument about generations could similarly be applied to a lot of long running game series too. Personally, I thought Saints Row 1-3 were much better games (including than SA), having improved on the series that clearly inspired them. The series is a brand name, seen as 'cool' and its name can certainly attract attention, but at this point I just don't see why. If this was releasing on PS6 at 60fps (to remove this hurdle) next week, I might be looking forwards to playing it at some point, but my anticipation would pale in comparison to if it were the next God of War, or Spiderman, or RE game (to give just 3 examples). 0 Show Comments Leave A Comment Hold on there, you need to login to post a comment...
